description: behavioral-spec.md's own header (lines 1-8) still declares 'revision: iteration 3, revised (spec review iteration-1 findings FIND-001..008 resolved AND spec review iteration-2 findings FIND-101..107 resolved -- see reviews/spec/iteration-1/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md and reviews/spec/iteration-2/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md for the full per-finding changelogs)', and the two structured Changelog tables immediately following (lines 10-41) only cover 'iteration 1 -> iteration 2' and 'iteration 2 -> iteration 3'. But the document's actual body text demonstrably incorporates resolutions through iteration 5 -- FIND-201 through FIND-206 (iteration 3's findings), FIND-301 through FIND-305 (iteration 4's), and FIND-401 through FIND-403 (iteration 5's) are all cited and resolved inline throughout REQ-105/106/108/109/112/113 -- yet none of these three iterations' worth of resolutions is ever summarized in a structured changelog table the way iterations 1 and 2 were, and RESOLUTION-NOTES.md files DO exist on disk for iterations 3, 4, and 5 (confirmed: reviews/spec/iteration-3/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md, iteration-4/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md, iteration-5/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md) but are never referenced from behavioral-spec.md's own header or changelog section the way iteration-1/2's are. A reader who trusts the document's own self-declared 'revision: iteration 3' framing and the promise that the changelog tables give 'the full per-finding changelog' has no single place in this document to look up what iterations 3, 4, or 5 individually changed -- they must grep the entire ~1760-line body for scattered 'resolves this revision's own FIND-XXX' phrases instead. This is a self-consistency/traceability gap in the document's own stated discipline, not a money-safety or concurrency defect -- but it is a real regression from the pattern the document itself established at iterations 1->2 and 2->3, and it directly undermines any reader's ability to use this document's own header as an accurate summary of its current state, which matters for a feature whose Dependencies/REQ-113 sections repeatedly stress the importance of never trusting a stale, frozen snapshot of a document's own state.

evidence.snippet: **revision**: iteration 3, revised (spec review iteration-1 findings FIND-001..008 resolved AND spec review iteration-2 findings FIND-101..107 resolved -- see `reviews/spec/iteration-1/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md` and `reviews/spec/iteration-2/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md` for the full per-finding changelogs) ... ## Changelog (iteration 1 -> iteration 2) ... ## Changelog (iteration 2 -> iteration 3)
